General.Description:
David Chen's parents ran a restaurant in the Richmond District of San Francisco. His father worked fourteen-hour days, six days a week. His mother kept the books, raised three children, and somehow found time to be the best cook in a kitchen full of professional cooks. They never asked for anything. They gave everything they had to give David and his sisters something they had never had: options.

David Chen's first business failed in eight months. His second lasted three years before being acquired for less than he needed it to sell for. His third became a mid-size software company with two hundred employees. His fourth — the one he is known for — disrupted the global logistics industry and made him one of the hundred wealthiest people in America.

He is still not entirely sure how any of it happened. From Nothing is his attempt to work it out — an autobiography that refuses to provide a template for success because, as Chen freely admits, most of what happened to him involved timing, luck, and decisions that looked wrong at the time and turned out to be right for reasons he did not understand until years later.

Honest, funny, and thoroughly unpretentious. Quietly essential.
